newsitem.title: PERU: Chronology of hostage dramas in South America.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of hostage dramas in South America.

text.p: The storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence by leftist Peruvian rebels who threatened on Wednesday to kill their high-profile hostages is the latest drama in a continent blighted by conflict.

The attack by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) was a major blow to President Alberto Fujimori's government, which had claimed virtual victory in a 16-year war on communist rebels belonging to the MRTA and the larger and better-known Maoist Shining Path.
Governments throughout Latin America have clashed with guerrilla groups for decades. The following is a chronology of some earlier guerrilla hostage-taking incidents:
Argentina

April 1996 - Inmates at an Argentine maximum security prison surrender 17 hostages and call off their week-old mutiny, clearing the way for copycat uprisings at other jails to end. At least 53 hostages were taken nationwide and a number of inmates were killed in the protests.
Brazil

July 9, 1994 - Inmates at Brazil's Central Prison in the southern city of Porto Alegre make a getaway with eight of their 24 hostages as shooting erupts in the streets. At least one police officer was killed.
Colombia
November 1985 - Colombia's M-19 guerrilla group, a nationalist, non-Marxist group founded in 1974, takes over Bogota's Palace of Justice and more than 100 people are killed in 27 hours of fighting.
March 1980 - M-19 takes over the Dominican Republic's embassy for two months with more than 30 hostages, 12 of them ambassadors, including the U.S. envoy. Some hostages were freed after one week.
Costa Rica
April 30, 1993 - A five-man kidnap gang is captured and their 23 hostages, including 18 Supreme Court justices, were freed by elite police.

March 1993 - A band of right-wing Nicaraguan guerrillas storm the Nicaraguan embassy in San Jose, taking 24 hostages including ambassador Alfonso Robelo. After a 13-day stand-off, they are paid $250,000 ransom and flown out of the country.
September 1992 - A lone Honduran gunman who kidnaps five people is paid a ransom and flown to Mexico before being shot to death during a separate kidnap bid in Belize.
El Salvador

November 1989 - Leftist guerrillas storm a Sheraton Hotel, taking a number of foreign military advisers hostage as well as 70 others for a harrowing 10 hours under unrelenting gunfire. There were no deaths reported.
Nicaragua

August 1993 - Rearmed Contra rebel fighters under the command of Jose Angel Talavera, alias "The Jackal," abduct 39 members of a government peace commission travelling in northern Nicaragua to negotiate the rebels' disarmament.

One day later, pro-Sandinista commandoes occupy the Managua headquarters of a leading right-wing political coalition, taking Vice President Virgilio Godoy and more than 30 others hostage. All of the hostages from both sides are released unharmed within a week.
August 1979 - FSLN guerrillas seize the National Palace, taking 40 parliamentarians and about 1,000 employees hostage.
